Manchester Brick Festival - Brick Festival Manchester Brick Festival July 11 @ 10:00 am - 4:00 pm Welcome to the Manchester Brick Festival! A LEGO fan event dedicated to all things brick! facts.semantic_text: Ritu in the Sun: Story Time - Stockport Council Join award-winning children’s author Moniza Hossain for a morning of fun! Location: Simply Books, 228 Moss Lane, Bramhall, SK7 1BD Fee: £15.99 Event Date and Time: 19/07/2026 11:00 - 12:00 Join award-winning children’s author Moniza Hossain for a morning of fun! Проверьте дату, время и бронирование перед планированием. Simply Books, 228 Moss Lane, Bramhall, SK7 1BD Join award-winning children’s author Moniza Hossain for a morning of fun! Moniza will read from her book, Ritu in the Sun, before leading a craft activity where kids can decorate hand cut-outs with their very own henna-style designs using glitter and coloured pens. Henna-style rub-on tattoos will also be available! A poetic text featuring stunning illustrations, Ritu in the Sun is a poignant story that is sure to inspire children to embrace their own unique beauty. Perfect for readers aged 4 and up Every ticket includes entry to the event for one parent and one child, as well as a copy of the book that Moniza will sign and dedicate For accessible transport options visit our accessible transport page

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A shotgun, handgun and ammunition were dug up by Greater Manchester Police from under a lawn at the house on Crowngreen Road, Eccles Police, who had been at the home since 8 July, used heavy machinery to search the garden, and also discovered a machete and a Class B drug from inside the home The force said a 57-year-old man and a 54-year-old woman were arrested earlier on suspicion of possession of a firearm and ammunition and taken into custody for questioning The force said the firearms were though to be viable, and have been "made safe and removed from the address for forensic testing" Det Sgt Gareth Bannister said: "Firearms have absolutely no place on our streets and the recovery of these items is significant in removing potentially lethal weapons from our communities "This is our message to those that look to use violence, intimidation and the threat of firearms to protect their criminal activities and interests – we will pursue you and bring you to justice."

And it's not quite got the same kind of vegetation [now]." He added: "Any time there's a fire it will kill lots and lots of fledglings, it will kill lots of mammals, it will kill lots of insects, and then it will create areas which are just no-go areas for years to come because there are no food plants." Convenience almost always won For journeys of only a couple of miles, many people now pause before starting the engine. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The doors have officially opened to a brand-new Community Diagnostic Centre (CDC) at Withington Community Hospital – the largest development on the site since the hospital opened 20 years ago The purpose-built Manchester and Trafford CDC will provide patients with quicker and more convenient access to a range of checks, scans and tests closer to home, reducing the need to travel to one of Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust’s (MFT) major hospital sites for rout Open 12 hours a day, seven days a week, the state-of-the-art centre is expected to deliver approximately 129,000 diagnostic tests this year, helping to reduce waiting times and support earlier diagnosis and treatment The Withington centre will operate alongside the existing CDCs in Harpurhey and Gorton, which have delivered more than 450,000 additional diagnostic tests since the programme launched in 2023 Patients will be able to access services following referral from their GP or another healthcare professional. Services available at the centre include audiology, cardiology, CT, DEXA, MRI, phlebotomy, respiratory tests, sleep studies, ultrasound and urology, among others The CDC will also be home to a new Children and Young People’s Asthma Diagnostic Pathway, giving eligible children aged five to 18 access to dedicated asthma diagnostic testing in a community setting

Residents living in all 10 boroughs will vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election on 30 July. We take a look at why it is happening, what the timetable is, and how the supplementary vote system works. Why is there an election? The election was triggered when Andy Burnham, who held the office for nine years, was elected the MP for Makerfield in last Thursday's parliamentary by-election. By law, an MP cannot sit in the House of Commons and hold a metropolitan mayor role that has powers over local policing. What is the timetable? The Greater Manchester mayoral contest has to take place within 35 days of the post becoming vacant. The nomination period for candidates for this election runs from 10:00 BST on 26 June to 16:00 on 3 July. The deadline for voter registration is midnight on 14 July. To have a postal vote in this election you must apply by 17:00 BST on Wednesday 15 July. The deadline to apply for a proxy vote is 17:00 BST on Wednesday 22 July. If you are already registered to vote by post, you will be sent a postal voting pack containing your ballot paper, which should arrive between 17 and 21 July. If you don't manage to post it in time you can return it by hand before 22:00 BST on polling day to your local electoral registration office or a polling station. And it's not quite got the same kind of vegetation [now]." He added: "Any time there's a fire it will kill lots and lots of fledglings, it will kill lots of mammals, it will kill lots of insects, and then it will create areas which are just no-go areas for years to come because there are no food plants." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Four Border Force officers involved in Manchester Airport custody death still suspended from duty Dad-of-two Karl Joyce was found unresponsive in a holding area after being arrested at the airport Comments News Greta Simpson Senior The full inquest into a man who died after being arrested at Manchester Airport almost 18 months ago remains more than six months away, it emerged today (July 13) Karl Joyce, 27, was arrested by Border Force officers while going through security at the airport on February 19 2025 Later that same day Mr Joyce, a father of two from Fleetwood in Lancashire, was found ‘slumped in a chair’ in a holding area. He was believed to have swallowed ‘wraps’ of cocaine found in his underwear , the M.E.N previously reported He was taken to Wythenshawe Hospital where he died of cocaine toxicity, an inquest opening into his death heard last August . An IOPC investigation was launched shortly after and the four officers involved were suspended pending a disciplinary review At a pre-inquest review hearing held at Manchester Coroner’s Court today, senior coroner Zack Golombeck moved the full inquest to begin on February 22 next year - more than two years on from Mr Joyce’s death

Marcus Smith was pronounced dead at the remote farm on Eccles Road, Whaley Bridge, in the early hours of May 1 2024 The budding footballer, who played for local club Chapel Town FC had sustained a fatal gunshot wound and died from his injuries. A second 19-year-old, who also suffered gunshot wounds on the same evening, was found nearby and treated in hospital before being discharged Police and forensics remained in attendance at the farm for a number of days following the shooting. Drone shots showed two police vans and four other unmarked vehicles parked beside the two-story farm near Whaley Bridge The homeowner on the property, a man aged in his 50s, was arrested on suspicion of murder and taken into police custody. It was revealed at the time that the shooting had happened during a suspected burglary incident He was then released on police bail as investigations into the incident continued. A 'significant level' of an over-the-counter medication was al Ms Mutch said it was likely Ms Allen-Gyves, who also taught geography at the school and was a member of its senior leadership team, was trying to 'manage down' her prescription at the same time as 'self-medicating' to try to sleep

And it all brutally came home for Carol Knight when she found out her car had been firebombed - and the culprits were never found Carol’s car was firebombed in May 2023 in Derker, Oldham , in what she believes was a targeted attack. At the time, her daughter, Angela Cosgrove, was running for re-election as a councillor for the St James ward which covers the area - and Carol believes it was linked to that But despite the damage, Carol says ‘nothing seemed to get done’ as a result. “The sad thing is people were afraid of opening up," she said. "People were frightened about things coming back onto them “I didn’t feel any reassurance. Nothing whatsoever that the police were going to look into it. A lot of people will have known because we had been here for 70 odd years and people said if they do not look after you, what will they do to us? “That to me told me and my husband if they can’t do anything, why can I be bothered? That to me said something needed to be desperately done.”

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter Oldham councillors have been warned the local authority could soon be breaking the law, as a top boss issues a warning. Elected members have been told they have two weeks to come up with someone to lead them or things could get much worse After no one was elected as Oldham Council’s leader on July 1, the local authority is still in limbo with officers continuing to use emergency powers just to keep services running . Key political decisions cannot be made and multiple meetings have been cancelled as a result The recent local elections on May 5 left no party with a majority or even a third of seats in the council chamber. Bids to lead the council put forward by Labour , Reform UK, and an alliance of different parties have all been rejected with everyone blaming each other for the dead Some progress has been made but the council is not able to function normally without a political leadership to drive the organisation forward. One councillor suggested to the Manchester Evening News the situation inside the council is now akin to ‘a poisoned lake’ View 2 Images Councillors meeting on July 1 (Image: Copyright Unknown)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police GMP to get £22m for extra police in Jewish communities in wake of Heaton Park synagogue attack The money will go towards putting on extra officers around schools, community centres and synagogues News Damon Wilkinson Reporter Greater Manchester Police is to get an extra £22m to pay for more police in Jewish communities in the wake of the Heaton Park synagogue terror attack The money will go towards putting on extra officers around schools, community centres and synagogues in areas such as Prestwich and Broughton. It will also fund specialist and plain-clothes officers trained to identify suspicious behaviour Announcing the move today (Monday) as part of a nationwide £250m boost to police budgets for tackling antisemitism , the Prime Minister said it was a ' step-change in protection and policing so Jewish communities can live and celebrate their faith free from fear' Crime and Policing Minister, Sarah Jones, added: "After a series of appalling attacks against Jewish communities, the difficult decision was made to raise the threat level to Severe. My thoughts remain with the victims of these vile attacks "Today we are going further and providing record funding to help keep Jewish people in Manchester safe, supporting visible policing and protection around synagogues, schools and community centres. We will do everything in our power to rid society of the evil of antisemitism."

The blaze has spread over the moorland and burned an area the size of at least 350 football pitches After the car crash on the A628, the road was closed off in both directions. An investigation is ongoing after the man was attacked on Hale Lane last Friday evening (June 19) The incident left the man fighting for his life. He remains in hospital for treatment today (June 26), GMP says. Four people have been arrested in connection with the incident over the past week Two men, aged 19 and 46, were arrested on suspicious of grievous bodily harm at an address on Firdale Road, Moston , later on Friday night. A 17-year-old boy was arrested on Saturday evening after he handed himself in at Ashton-under-Lyne police station And a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of theft and assault in connection with the investigation on Monday. All four suspects have since been bailed pending further enquiries Enquiries have remained ongoing throughout the week. Anyone with information is asked to call GMP on 0161 856 8906 or 0161 856 9080, quoting log 3924-19/6/26, or contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111

But for decades the Collier Street baths in Greengate has been an empty decaying shell Now it could have a new lease of life as Mackie Mayor style food hall which is housed in another historic building - Manchester's former Smithfield Market Hall on the edge of the Northern Quarter The listed former baths, built in 1855, is situated in the Colliers Yard development which was the former medieval heart of Salford. Renaker secured planning permission to build three tower blocks in 2020 on condition that the baths were restored The Cortland block was completed in October 2023 - a 50-storey tower with 559 rental apartments. Manchester Crown Court heard how Kaelun Howe, 22, burgled - and attempted to burgle - numerous premises in the days leading up to the robbery at the bookie In April this year, he turned up at a man's house and pointed a gun at him through the peephole. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford RSPCA responds after social media video shows dog chained up in Salford WARNING: This article contains images some readers may find upsetting News James Holt Senior Live and Breaking News Reporter 16:32, 05 Jul 2026 View 2 Images The RSPCA has The RSPCA has responded after a social media video appeared to show a dog trying to escape out of a chain in a yard in Salford . A clip, shared online, appeared to show the white dog trying to wriggle out of the collar with claims made that it was 'kept chained up at a scrapyard' A post by dog trainer and animal welfare campaigner Sammy Wilkinson received hundreds of responses and comments after it was shared on Thursday (July 2). "I've just watched with my own eyes this dog nearly choke himself to death trying to escape the chain," he wrote The clip, filmed in Swinton , zoomed in to show the animal appearing to be repeatedly struggling and wrestling with the collar and chain. It was claimed that the incident had been reported to the RSPCA However, a further update on social media then claimed that the owners had 'agreed to let the dog go if we can find a suitable home for him.' In a response, the RSPCA said it was 'aware of the situation' but could not comment on individual complaints or what action may or may not have been taken. It went on to encourage members of the public to report any other concerns about animals and their welfare

Leading detectives on the case said he will spend the rest of his days in prison The first survivor came forward in 2019 to police, reporting offences that occurred when they were a child. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Police issue statement after swan killed by car in front of her mate and cygnets at Salford beauty spot WARNING: Distressing image of the scene in Salford below Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 13:47, 26 Jun 2026 Updated 13:52, 26 Jun 2026 The death of a female swan in front of her mate and their cygnets is being investigated by police The bird was hit and run over by a car near a car park close to a pond at a popular beauty spot in Salford . Police have now issued an appeal for the public's help - describing it as an 'awful incident'. It's understood the car involved, possibly a Ford, didn't stop at the scene An upsetting photograph showing the dead swan lying on the road with her mate and their brood of six cygnets, together with a car in the background, is being shared widely on social media The tragedy has sparked anger and outrage in the community, with people flocking to the scene to check on the male swan and the cygnets. It happened at Queensmere Dam, off Queensway in Swinton The lake and the fish in it are managed by the Swinton and Pendlebury Anglers club. Club bailiff Jay Dixon said: "We have had thousands and thousands of messages about this. It is shocking. I just do not understand it. You cannot miss a large swan."

Sadly, he was found dead at around 5pm on Sunday (July 19) A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said his family has been informed. They are being supported by specialist officers Dozens of tributes for Michael, who was known as Mikey, have since been shared on social media since the news of his death. Michael was a boxer, the Manchester Evening News understands, and often posted about his fights on social media

A 'significant level' of an over-the-counter medication was al Ms Mutch said it was likely Ms Allen-Gyves, who also taught geography at the school and was a member of its senior leadership team, was trying to 'manage down' her prescription at the same time as 'self-medicating' to try to sleep

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Derker 'The police knocked on every house on our road and not one of them would give any information' Life in Derker being a 'nightmare' is now over after a major police crackdown but there are fears a 'golden opportunity' is being wasted Comments New It was an area riddled with fear and violence. And it all brutally came home for Carol Knight when she found out her car had been firebombed - and the culprits were never found Carol’s car was firebombed in May 2023 in Derker, Oldham , in what she believes was a targeted attack. At the time, her daughter, Angela Cosgrove, was running for re-election as a councillor for the St James ward which covers the area - and Carol believes it was linked to that But despite the damage, Carol says ‘nothing seemed to get done’ as a result. “The sad thing is people were afraid of opening up," she said. "People were frightened about things coming back onto them “I didn’t feel any reassurance. Nothing whatsoever that the police were going to look into it. A lot of people will have known because we had been here for 70 odd years and people said if they do not look after you, what will they do to us? “That to me told me and my husband if they can’t do anything, why can I be bothered? That to me said something needed to be desperately done.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Greater Manchester's latest air quality map shows impact of raging moor fires across every borough It comes as residents living in the shadow of both fires have complained about the side-effects of the smoke Comments News Charlotte Fisher Report Two major incidents have been declared amid the fires at Dovestone and Swineshaw Reservoir , in Greenfield in Oldham and at Tintwistle Moor near Glossop. Dozens of firefighters remain at both scenes as smoke continues to billow into the air over our region On Wednesday, Paul Fearnhead, Incident Commander at the Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS), described the area near Dovestone as 'really, really challenging' as the 'extensive wildfire' continued He said: "Currently we have around just short of ten fire engines, including our wildfire capabilities at this scene and they’re deployed across the moorlands in this warm weather , which is being hampered by smoke and wind "If you're a member of the public in the area, we are asking you to stay away. It's a small area for us to work in, and the moors at this time are very smoky, and we'd ask you not to come across this area." Both fires are sending huge plumes of smoke across our region and beyond - with the latest air quality maps today (July 16) showing the ongoing impact the fires are having across Greater Manchester

The investment arm of the insurance firm Aviva want to build a new logistics hub on land next to the existing Atlas Business Park, off Simonsway It will see the creation of around 40,000 square metres of industrial, warehouse and logistics space, and supporting offices, for a 'range of occupiers', the firm says Its proximity to the M56 motorway, Manchester Airport and Manchester city centre mean it is an 'ideal location' for such businesses, they said, estimating it could be worth £44m to the region's economy Part of the site was formerly a factory for the now defunct electrical engineering firm Ferranti. Aviva first outlined their plans for the site, which is close to Heald Green and Manchester's border with Stockport , in 2022. He said United Utilities were investigating to determine the exact cause He added: “I have asked council officers to make it clear to United Utilities that this is the second or third time this area has been dug up and the road has had to be closed “Residents deserve a proper, long-term fix rather than repeated disruption, and I have asked that they fully resolve the problem this time. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Major road closure update after car bursts into flames and spreads to moorland The A628 Woodhead Pass remains shut after the crash on Thursday News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 08:38, 18 Jul 2026 View 2 Images The scene of the b A major road over moorland near Greater Manchester will remain shut until at least Monday following a car fire The car burst into flames on a stretch of the A628 Woodhead Pass between the A57 at Hollingworth and A616 at Flouch on Thursday afternoon (July 16). Shocking photos from the scene showed a black car completely engulfed in a blaze Smoke and flames could be seen billowing from the vehicle, which had left the road and crashed on adjacent moorland just after 1.30pm. The fire then spread to adjacent moorland, a South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said The crash came amid the major moorland fire in Tintwistle, above Woodhead Road, which first broke out round three weeks ago . The blaze has spread over the moorland and burned an area the size of at least 350 football pitches After the car crash on the A628, the road was closed off in both directions. National Highways has now confirmed in an update that the closure is expected to remain in place until at least Monday morning

Manchester Crown Court heard how Kaelun Howe, 22, burgled - and attempted to burgle - numerous premises in the days leading up to the robbery at the bookie In April this year, he turned up at a man's house and pointed a gun at him through the peephole. "I'm going to shoot you," he said Later that afternoon, Howe forced his way into the William Hill at Salford precinct, armed with what appeared to be a gun, but turned out to be a BB gun. The cashier moved into a safe room behind glass before Howe shot at it He then climbed onto the counter and stole the contents of the till His terrifying attacks ended when he was arrested at Manchester Airport. Howe has now been jailed for six years and nine months for a string of burglary and robbery offences

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 12:24, 15 Jul 2026 View 2 Images P Campaigners have escalated a row with Manchester council over the future of Ryebank Fields in Chorlton . Plans to build 120 homes on the land were submitted last February by Manchester Metropolitan University (MMU) alongside housing developers Step Places and the Southway Housing A group known as the Ryebank Fields Community Group (RFCG) submitted an alternative application in August to ‘protect’ the land and use it as a community woodland and meadow. No decision has been made yet on either planning application Ryebank Fields Community Group said its submission to protect the land was supposed to be decided by the council in December but they are still waiting for an outcome. The group has written an open letter to town hall chief executive Tom Stannard asking for an explanation The letter reads: "We have contacted Manchester City Council on seven separate occasions seeking an update, a timetable for determination, and clarification of whether any outstanding matters remain "We have also offered a telephone conversation and a video meeting to assist in resolving any issues and facilitate progress. Despite these efforts, we have received neither a clear timetable for determination nor a satisfactory explanation for the continuing delay

evidence_packet.source_url:

Registration needed: https:/conexen.net/conexen-events/conexen-manchester-july/

Welcome to CONEXEN Manchester – A warm and welcoming community for professionals and founders in biopharma, life sciences, and health tech in Manchester! Here, we invite you to join us for an informal and friendly gathering where connections are made, knowledge is shared, and friendships are formed. Come with an open heart and a willingness to “listen” rather than “sell.”

​​We will be hosting our Manchester event at the amazing space of Cloud 23 Cocktail Bar. It is a casual setting where we can come together, exchange greetings, engage in conversation, and simply enjoy a pleasant time.

​​Picture this as more than just an event, it’s a life sciences community gathering. Our focus is on providing you with an opportunity to meet fellow professionals and founders in a relaxed and amiable environment. We’ll share conversations over delicious food and drinks, and leave with a sense of excitement and a pocketful of new contacts and ideas.

​​Join us for an evening surrounded by incredible people, and let’s make it a night to remember. Looking forward to sharing good company and creating memorable connections!

​Theme: The Forces Reshaping Work & Culture in Life Sciences.

Join a focused discussion led by Paul Bradley-Law on the forces redefining culture in a hybrid world. Our panellists will explore how hybrid working, evolving HR trends, leadership style, and a multi-generational workforce are reshaping how organisations operate, alongside the growing influence of AI in the workplace.

We’ll examine how trust is built through clarity and candour in uncertain times—without defaulting to micromanagement—and how to address “proximity bias” to ensure fair visibility, recognition, and opportunity across distributed teams.

Join peers shaping the North-West Life Sciences ecosystem and driving the region’s growing influence.

​Moderator: Paul Bradley-Law (Founder, The Great People Machine)

​Panelists:

  • Ike Cooke, Business Growth & Commercialisation Manager, LYVA Labs

  • Julia Buckler, Senior Director, Site Head, Qiagen

​The format of the night:

  • ​18:00 Doors open – drinks, networking and meeting great people.

  • ​18:30 Talks start

  • ​19:15 Drinks, food and networking.

  • ​20:30 End of the night – you leave with new contacts and fresh ideas.

​​Venue: Cloud 23 Cocktail Bar – The Manchester Deansgate Hotel, 303 Deansgate, Manchester M3 4LQ, United Kingdom.

This event is proudly supported by Nexa Life Sciences and Kadans Science Partner, hosted by Kadans Science Partner.

​

​And finally…

​This is a ticketed event. Food and drinks for the night are included.

​Please let your colleagues and industry friends know about us, we hope to build it into a great resource for the ecosystem over the coming months and years. Attendance will be taken at this event. If you register but don’t show up, this has a knock-on effect on event arrangements. If it happens 3 times, we may need to reconsider your participation. This is simply a measure to allow appropriate respect to the organisers, speakers, sponsors, and your fellow Conexers.

​See you there!

​Ashley, Julia, and Sajid
Manchester Organisers

​Tickets FAQs: https:/www.conexen.net/faq

From sensitive data being shared with public AI tools to evolving regulatory requirements, organisations must ensure AI is being deployed responsibly, securely and with appropriate oversight. In this webinar, Brian Martin is joined by Seán Brennan, CRA Practice Manager, Integrity360, to explore how organisations can confidently adopt AI while managing governance, risk and compliance. Drawing on emerging frameworks including ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the EU AI Act, this session will provide practical guidance on establishing governance for both internally developed AI solutions and the use of public AI platforms. Attendees will gain insight into managing AI-related risks, protecting sensitive information, meeting emerging regulatory expectations, and creating a framework that enables innovation without compromising security or compliance. Join us for a practical discussion on how to build effective AI governance that balances innovation with trust, accountability and risk management. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Childhood friends raise $1m for Manchester startup BidScript Posted on July 2, 2026 by staff Childhood friends raise $1m for Manchester startup BidScript Henry Brogan & Tyler McCarthy launched business while still at university to address fundamental flaw in bidding of public & private contracts Share: Founders Investment Two childhood friends have now raised $1 million for their Manchester-based AI startup BidScript. Henry Brogan and Tyler McCarthy launched the AI tender management business while still at university to address a fundamental flaw in the bidding of public and private contracts. Hundreds of billions of pounds of public and private contracts are awarded each year, yet most businesses are still completing tenders manually, using highly time-consuming spreadsheets and shared drives.
